spec.name: reference
spec.why: Noiseless, moderate ellipticity, no PA offset, interpolation everywhere. The cleanest measurement of the scale, and the case every other one perturbs.

spec.name: single_mode_control
spec.why: The reference ring with only one harmonic planted. Separates a tool's ability to recover an isolated mode from its ability to recover one mode out of several, which the pilot showed are different questions for photutils and not for the other two.

spec.name: interpolate_default
spec.why: AutoProf's own default sampling. The single largest effect on the grid; with the reference case this is the whole 0.1%-versus-13-25% story.

spec.name: eps_circular
spec.why: At eps ~ 0 polar angle and eccentric anomaly coincide, so the angle-basis question vanishes and every other difference is isolated.

spec.name: eps_high
spec.why: Strong ellipticity, where the basis difference bites hardest.

spec.name: pa_30
spec.why: A non-zero position angle is what makes AutoProf's sky-frame polar basis differ from the major-axis frame, so it is what tests the n*PA rotation.

spec.name: isoclip_off
spec.why: Puts AutoProf on the eccentric-anomaly basis, where the same-order rotation is not a valid conversion. Measured to show the size of the error it would make.

spec.name: background_offset
spec.why: A constant added to the image. Raw amplitudes must be unchanged; AutoProf's native coefficients must move by the ring-mean ratio and the reconstruction must cancel it exactly.

spec.name: noise_snr100
spec.why: Mild noise, several realizations. One realization measures a realization.

spec.name: noise_snr30
spec.why: Harder noise, several realizations; sets the scatter the tolerances answer to.

spec.name: radius_x_interpolate
spec.why: Interpolation start is itself a radius threshold, so a ring's sampling mode is decided by both factors jointly and neither alone predicts it. This setting puts the switch between two different pairs of radii than the default does, so one radius set spans three switch positions across the grid.

spec.name: eps_x_basis
spec.why: High ellipticity on the eccentric-anomaly basis: the cell where order mixing is predicted to be worst, and the one that settles whether that path can be converted.

spec.name: pa_x_resampling
spec.why: A non-zero PA without polar resampling. The rotation the conversion applies is derived for the resampled path only; this is the cell that shows what it costs to apply it anywhere else.

spec.name: noise_x_clipping
spec.why: Sigma clipping removes samples asymmetrically around a ring, so its effect on a harmonic is not the effect of noise alone. Clipping off, at the noisier level.

spec.name: combined_stress
spec.why: Every axis at its hardest setting at once. A check that nothing falls over, not a measurement: with several factors moving together it cannot attribute a discrepancy, which is exactly why the rest of the grid is one factor at a time.

spec.name: psf_set_8
spec.why: Double the assumed PSF with the interpolation setting still at 100. The threshold doubles to 800 px, every ring stays interpolated, and every ratio must be unchanged. A null result by construction -- which is the point, since it shows ap_set_psf acts through the threshold and nowhere else.

spec.name: psf_x_interpolate
spec.why: Default interpolation setting with a doubled PSF, putting the switch at 40 px instead of 20. Rings change sampling mode without the interpolation setting changing at all.

spec.name: threshold_matched_control
spec.why: Interpolation setting 10 with a halved PSF: different option values from the default arm in both factors, and the identical 20 px threshold. Every ring must return the identical ratio. This is the sharpest form of the claim -- only the product matters, not either factor.

archive_note: Per-realization rows beyond the first 1 are summarized rather than stored; 96 were dropped. Every claim is computed from the 'summary' block, which is complete. The dropped rows are regenerable exactly: the run is deterministic given the recorded seed block. The full untrimmed run is in outputs/benchmark_harmonic_scale/.
